system.description:
1st Level Clan Feature

You were born with no special family name. No bloodline. No Hijutsu. No Kekkei Genkai. You were born with nothing, but the unending drive for greatness beyond those who were born with it all. You wake up every day with one goal in mind. To surpass everyone else. You accomplish this in two distinct ways, your Drive and your Style.

Drive

Your grit and tenacity in combat is called your Drive, a measure of you building momentum, focus and experience through an encounter. You begin each combat with 0 Drive, and can accumulate up to 1 + Your Proficiency bonus at any given time, resetting to 0 when combat ends.

You gain 1 Drive, when you deal damage to, or take damage from a hostile creature. You can only gain Drive, in either way, once each, until the start of your next turn.

Feature cannot grant you Drive more than once before the start of each of your next turns, unless otherwise specified.

As you build Drive, over the course of combat, you gain passive bonuses based on that accumulated value, can spend it on effects and abilities that call for it. You cannot gain Drive as part of the same action or feature that you spend Drive on.

Momentum Shift – 2+ Drive: Once per turn, when you deal or take damage, you can move up to half your speed, without provoking opportunity attacks and can spend 1 Drive to either; Use a skill-based action, Use the Help action or make one unarmed or weapon attack against a creature in range (Pick one).

Drive Dice – 4+ Drive: Once per turn, you can spend 2 Drive to add a d4 to provide a bonus or penalty to any attack roll, damage roll, or Ability or skill check made by an ally or hostile creature within 30 feet of you. This die is added before the roll resolves. Once you add a bonus or penalty dice to a creatures result, you cannot do so again, for that creature, until the end of your next turn. The power of this penalty increases to a d6 at 11th level.

Apex Drive – 6+ Drive: Your unlock your styles Apex effect, for the remainder of combat.

Style

At character creation, select one of the following Styles.. This Style determines how you generate Drive and what unique abilities you have to spend your Drive on. Each Style grants you a way to generate Drive, a unique special ability and your Apex Drive. This choice cannot be changed later.

Blazing Style. Embodied by those who fights with unmatched aggression and focus (Ex. Rock Lee, Might Guy, Zabuza). Attacks you make gain Pierce 4.

Drive Charge: You can gain 2 Drive on a critical hit.

Blazing Surge: As a bonus action, you can spend 2 Drive, converting it into a single charge of an expendable resource your class has (Genjutsu Specialist: Actualization Die, Hunter-Nin: Combat Exploit forgoing Lethal Attack die, Medical-Nin: Domain Charges, etc.).

Apex Drive: When you unlock this effect, select one hostile creature, and select one Damage type or condition. Damage you deal ignores resistance of the chosen damage type. The target creature cannot make saving throws to resist the chosen condition at advantage.

Adamant Style. Embodied by those who endure what others cannot (Sakura, Tsunade). For every Drive you have at the beginning of each of your turns, you gain +2 Temporary hit points. If you have temporary hit points granted by another effect when this feature would activate, you instead gain half of the listed amount, adding it to your current temporary hit point value

Drive Charge: You can gain 2 Drive when you reduce a triggering damage source by half or more.

Enduring Surge: As a Bonus Action, you can spend 2 Drive, selecting one creature you can see within 30 feet of you, until the end of your next turn, the first time each turn you take damage from this creature, reduce the number of damage dice rolled by 1. This increases to 2 at 7th and 3 15th levels.

Apex Drive: You refuse to fall in battle, you must endure. Each time you would fail a saving throw, you can spend 1 Drive to gain a rank of Mastery to the result. You can do this twice per failure.

Guiding Star Style. Embodied by those whose strength multiplies through the bonds they share with their allies (Iruka, Shizune, Sai). All allied creatures, excluding yourself, within 15 feet of you gain a +2 bonus to their damage rolls as your presence sharpen their focus. This increases to +4 at 11th level.

Drive Charge You can gain 2 Drive when you support an allied creature, other than yourself by increasing or restoring any dice-based result (Attack, Damage, Save, etc.), any statistic they have (DR, HP, Chakra, etc.) or reducing incoming damage they take. Other supportive effects can trigger this at GM’s discretion such as interposing an attack or interrupting a harmful jutsu.

Guiding Surge: As a bonus action, you can spend 2 Drive, selecting one allied creature. That creature can reroll the next 2 dice rolls they make. Once a creature benefits from this surge, they cannot do so again until they complete a short rest. This increases to 3 dice rolls at 11th level.

Apex Drive: You can use the Help Action targeting any allied creature, as a Bonus action, so long as they are within 60 feet of you. Additionally, when a creature benefits from this Help action, you gain temporary chakra points equal to half your level. You can only temporary chakra in this way, once per creature assisted, per short rest.

Shogi Style. Embodied by those who win battles through preparation, positioning and anticipation before a fight begins. (Temari, Hayate, Jiraiya). Ninja tools you used such as Explosive Tools, Medical Tools, Toolkits, Poisons or Scrolls can be used as a Bonus Action, if their normal use requires an Action.

Drive Charge: You can gain 2 Drive when a hostile creature gains a Condition.

Tactical Surge: As a bonus action, you can spend 2 Drive, to summon any one; Weapon, Explosive Tool, Trap, Toolkit, Communication Tool, Blank Keycard or Data Scroll of a rank you can access normally. These Ninja tools can be used once before breaking or expiring or 1 hour has passed, whichever occurs first.

Apex Drive: You always overprepare and overdeliver. Once per creature, per rest, when you cast a Jutsu you know, that you have not previously cast this combat, you can shock your opponent with the gravity of the technique. If they attempt to spend their Reaction in response to the Jutsu, its effects or as part of making or failing a saving throw, you can spend your Reaction, causing them to lose their Reaction.
